To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the dominant three-loop corrections to the lightest CP-even Higgs boson in supersymmetric models can be as large as 3 Gev, (2) the three-loop corrections are significant in the parameter space that is currently favored by naturalness and collider bounds, and (3) the three-loop contributions can lower the required top squark masses by as much as a factor of two.

(i) the Higgs bosons mass is 126.2±0.4 GeV, (ii) this mass can be obtained with 3 TeV top squark masses, (iii) the dominant three-loop contributions are O(10) GeV and are of opposite sign to those of the two-loop contributions, (iv) the top squark mass is not the only parameter that can be varied, and (v) there are many viable models that can be tested at the
the Higgs bosons mass can be raised by as much as ∼3 GeV by the three-loop top-squark corrections, and this can lower the required top squark mass from 10 TeV to 3- 4 TeV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the Higgs mass in supersymmetric models.
the calculation of three-loop corrections to the lightest Higgs mass and their impact on the top-squark mass in supersymmetric models.
supersymmetric models of particle physics, and the implications of the Higgs bosons mass on the masses of the supersymmetric particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a 125.6  GeV Higgs mass is compatible with a top squark mass of 3-4  TeV in the simplest supersymmetric models.
, in the simplest supersymmetric model, a top squark of 3 TeV is not ruled out by the 125.7 GeV Higgs mass, but is disfavored by other constraints.
, if the Higgs bosons mass lies between 125.5 and 126 GeV, the top squarks must lie between 3 and 4 TeV, and the gluinos between 1.2 and 1.6 TeV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have found that the top-squark mass scale required by the Higgs mass is reduced to 3-5 TeV for the minimal supersymmetric model with a universal scalar mass at the grand unified theory scale and a moderate tan  β.
three-loop contributions to Higgs boson masses are not negligible in supersymmetric models, and they should be included in future analyses.

, with the three-loop corrections taken into account, the 125.9 GeV Higgs mass is consistent with top squarks of O(3) TeV in a large region of the parameter space of the MSSM, and the LHC can probe the entire parameter space with a 14 TeV center-of-mass energy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Higgs bosons mass is a poor predictor of supersymmetry at colliders.
the three-loop terms are large and should not be ignored.
the Higgs bosons mass is not a reliable probe for top squark masses in the multi-TeV range.
